Q: Update join query in Spring Boot A:

HQL/JPQL bulk updates don't support this syntax:

update SensorStats s
join SensorTemp ...
join SensorLast ...
set ...

For PostgreSQL, use a native query. PostgreSQL supports UPDATE ... FROM, which fits this case quite well:

@Modifying(clearAutomatically = true)
@Transactional
@Query(value = """
    UPDATE sensor_stats s
    SET
        nb_updates = s.nb_updates + 1,
        first_update = COALESCE(s.first_update, young.last_update)
    FROM sensor_temp young
    JOIN sensor_last old ON old.id = young.id
    WHERE s.id = young.id
      AND old.last_update IS DISTINCT FROM young.last_update
    """, nativeQuery = true)
int incUpdatesFromTempTable();

Use your actual table/column names, of course.

Use:

old.last_update IS DISTINCT FROM young.last_update

instead of:

old.last_update <> young.last_update

because IS DISTINCT FROM also behaves correctly if one of the values is NULL.

Also, clearAutomatically = true is useful here because bulk updates happen directly in the database and Hibernate's persistence context may otherwise still contain stale SensorStats entities.

I hope it can help you fix your issue.

Q: How to get a dependency's MAJOR version in CMake (for ffmpeg)? A:

As far as I know ffmpeg does not expose a single version macro.
This is because ffmpeg is a "collection" of related but separate libraries:
libavcodec, libavdevice, libavutil etc.

Instead each library in ffmpeg introduces its own version macro.

E.g. for libavutil you have (see here - requires #include "libavutil/version.h"):

#define     LIBAVUTIL_VERSION_MAJOR   56  // here would be your actual version

(there are similar LIBAVCODEC_VERSION_MAJOR etc.).

You can use these macros in your code directly (by #includeing the relevant version.h file) - no need for CMake support.

If you need to check a range of versions you can apply simple boolean logic to macros.
E.g. if you want to check if a version is 7.0 or higher, you can do the following:

#if LIBAVUTIL_VERSION_MAJOR >= 70
  // ... something
#else
  // ... something else
#endif

Here is a short demo of using the preprocessor to check if a #defined macro is >= some value: Demo - Godbolt

Q: Struggling to understand how to have some text inside an unordered list bold A:

The understanding that having a <b> tag inside an <li> was not legal came from this Stack Overflow question

That's not what the answer there says. Read it more carefully. It says:

A b element may not be a child of a ul element

It then goes onto say that the OP's first example, where <b> is a child of <li> is correct.

So your concerns are unfounded, I think you just misread the answer.

Q: Can't exclude directories from .htaccess mobile redirect? A:

Your second RewriteCond is almost there I think. Try something like this:

RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !^/?(directory1|directory2)($|/)

Place as many directories as you need in directory1|directory2|etc.

This should come out to "if REQUEST_URI does not begin with /directory1 or /directory2."

It will match:

  • /directory1/dasdas
  • /directory1
  • /directory1/

etc

Which I think is what you want.
